newsitem.title: USA: Columbia practices under review by firm.
newsitem.headline: Columbia practices under review by firm.

text.p: Adding to pressures facing Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp, a Washington, D.C., law firm working with private insurers said Thursday it is reviewing Columbia's billing and marketing practices.
"We are engaged in reviewing the billing and marketing practices" of Columbia/HCA, said Allison Duncan, a partner at the private law firm of Wiley Rein & Fielding.
"We are working with a number of insurers to that end," Duncan said in an interview.
Wall Street analysts said they had expected Columbia to begin facing more private-sector scrutiny once the federal investigation of the company got rolling.
"The next shoe to drop in this would be -- does a commercial insurer step in here with a civil lawsuit?" said one healthcare industry analyst who asked not to be named.

Eleven shareholder lawsuits have been filed against officers and directors of the Nashville, Tenn.-based hospital company since federal agents in March began looking into its billing practices for laboratory and other work.

Three mid-level executives of the largest U.S. for-profit hospital firm were indicted Wednesday on charges of fraud in an alleged billing scam. Unnamed federal officials were quoted in press reports saying that more indictments could come.
Earlier this month, the federal probe that started in El Paso, Texas, widened dramatically when federal agents seized files at 33 Columbia facilities in six states.

On Friday, dissatisfaction among Columbia board members with the handling of the probe and other issues led to the resignation of long-time Columbia chief executive and chairman Richard Scott, as well as president David Vandewater.
Scott was replaced by vice chairman Dr. Thomas Frist.
